question: A 32-year-old woman with a recurrent vesicular genital rash comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of a painful, pruritic rash that began on the extremities and has spread to her trunk. Her only medication is acyclovir. Her temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). Examination of the skin shows several reddish-purple papules and macules, some of which have a dusky center with a lighter ring around them. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Recurrent vesicular genital rash" -> "Painful, pruritic rash spreading from extremities to trunk" -> "Reddish-purple papules and macules with dusky center and lighter ring" -> "Fever of 38.1°C" -> "Acyclovir medication" -> "Herpes simplex virus infection" -> "Possible diagnosis: Eczema herpeticum" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Recurrent vesicular genital rash" -> "Painful, pruritic rash spreading from extremities to trunk" -> "Reddish-purple papules and macules with dusky center and lighter ring" -> "Fever of 38.1°C" -> "Acyclovir medication" -> "Herpes simplex virus infection" -> "Erythema multiforme" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation with a recurrent vesicular genital rash, along with the current painful, pruritic rash spreading from extremities to trunk, and the presence of reddish-purple papules and macules with dusky centers and lighter rings, is highly suggestive of erythema multiforme. Erythema multiforme is a hypersensitivity reaction typically triggered by infections or medications, such as acyclovir in this case.
